speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, please tell me how many loose stools you have passed in the last 24 hours and if you have experienced any fever or blood in your stool.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). Given the recent use of levofloxacin, the high frequency of watery stools, and abdominal cramping, this presentation is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. I will proceed with a stool test for C. difficile toxins to confirm this.
